- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike in sentiment, apply a 10–15% downward correction to prevent overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average to reduce mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +1.0 and -0.3), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and forecast is drifting away from recent 18-day mean, align forecast to mean to avoid drift bias.
